Provenance of the coordinate fixtures named tab-real-*.

source.txt is, byte for byte, the Tab.hs file generated by
capture-evidence.sh (audit section 6.1). Each span.json is the "span"
object GHC 9.14.1 itself reported for the "s" literal in one deliberate
type error, run as:

    ghc -fno-code -fdiagnostics-as-json Tab.hs

captured 2026-10-04 on x86_64 Linux (GHC 9.14.1, cabal-install 3.16.1.0).
Only the span objects were recorded verbatim, not the whole JSON lines.

expected.txt gives the character offsets of the literal, found by
searching the source text for it, NOT by running the code under test.

What the six cases establish (each reports a different column under
each competing rule):

    baseline    no tab                         start column 5
    col5        tab at column 5                start column 9  (one-column rule: 6)
    col1        tab at column 1                start column 9  (one-column rule: 2)
    col7        tab at column 7                start column 9  (one-column rule: 8)
    col9        tab at column 9                start column 17 (one-column rule: 10)
    multibyte   2-byte character before a tab  start column 9  (byte counting: 17)

Conclusions: columns count characters, not bytes; a tab advances to the
next multiple of 8 plus 1; a span's end column is exclusive.
Still to be re-captured on GHC 9.10.x and 9.12.x.
